$comment: The first catalogue release covers one archetype, not all 1440 modules (MVP Architecture §16.3). Israeli B2B wholesale distribution: order to cash, procure to pay, stock, and the Israeli accounting boundary.
editionNote: AIOne delivers Odoo 19 Enterprise. The Foundation mounts both the core and the Enterprise revisions, and a solution workspace defaults to target_odoo_edition 'enterprise'. The scope below therefore includes Enterprise modules, and a capability built from them is an Enterprise capability. Scoping only core modules would make the catalogue describe a product AIOne does not sell — every requirement that Enterprise answers would appear as a gap.
notes: Modules listed here are the business-selected set. Their transitive dependencies come from the release and are recorded as technical dependencies, not as scope decisions (Blueprint §13).
Nothing here asserts that a module satisfies a requirement. That is a fit assessment, made per requirement against verified capabilities.
l10n_il_reports depends on account_reports, which depends on account_accountant, both Enterprise. Naming the localization without them described a module set that cannot install.

Deliberately outside this scope at this release: stock_barcode, web_studio, documents, sign, sale_subscription, sale_renting, the marketplace connectors and the delivery carriers. Each is Enterprise and available, and none is reached by a requirement the Quick Start interview produces — QS-08 asks about warehouses, tracking, dropshipping, imports and returns, and never about barcode scanning. A scope entry is a commitment to author and verify capabilities for a module, so an unreachable module is left out rather than listed. stock_barcode belongs here as soon as the comprehensive interview asks about warehouse operations.
